subject: Velora Prod: sudden 5xx/429 spike — need immediate mitigation and exec alignment
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@velora.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T09:12:00Z
Subject: [Urgent] Production 5xx spike and timeouts - Velora Prod - us-west-2

Hannah / Marissa,

We're seeing a sudden burst of 5xx errors and client timeouts across our Velora production workspace in us-west-2 starting ~08:50 PDT. Error breakdown from our side: ~18% 5xx (mostly 502/503), ~12% 429s, and overall p95 latency up from 220ms to ~2.3s. This is impacting payment reconciliation — queue is backing up and retries are amplifying.

We've already opened a support ticket (INC-89321). Attaching a short sample of logs (pod-logs-20270607.txt). Can you confirm if this is a known scheduled maintenance or capacity issue on your side? We need an ETA on a fix or recommended mitigation (e.g., route to a fallback model or temporary rate-limiting on our side).

Oliver
Ops Lead — Velora

Attachments:
- pod-logs-20270607.txt (text log excerpt, 120KB)

Date: 2027-06-07T09:26:18Z
Subject: Re: [Urgent] Production 5xx spike and timeouts - Velora Prod - us-west-2

Thanks Oliver — we're on it. Looping in infra (Marcus), scaling/serving (Neha), and account (Marissa) for coordination. Initial asks: 1) Marcus/Neha, can you triage the dedicated pool for Velora in us-west-2 (pool id: velora-dedicated-usw2) and check node provisioning latency and recent autoscaler events? 2) Marcus, please check cloud provider events (spot reclaim, AZ imbalance) + recent kernel errors. 3) I'll keep Velora updated and coordinate an exec note if this becomes a breach.

Immediate mitigation options to consider:
- Enable fallback routing of a portion of traffic to the hosted pool for non-sensitive requests.
- Temporarily increase autoscaler aggressive headroom (buffer nodes) for the Velora pool.
- Short-term rate-limit on high-retry clients to prevent retry amplification.

I attached their logs from Oliver. We need status in 15 minutes for a customer-facing update.

- Hannah
Senior Customer Ops — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: [Urgent] Production 5xx spike and timeouts - Velora Prod - us-west-2

Quick triage update (0-20m):
- Observed behavior: autoscaler struggled to bring new inference nodes online. Provision latency spiked ~60-95s (normal ~12-20s). During that window, request backlog rose and the serving runtime started returning 502/503 as GPU workers exhausted their KV caches and queued requests timed out.
- Root signals: two contributing factors: (1) one of the AZs in us-west-2 experienced increased spot reclaim chatter which delayed node allocation; (2) our autoscaler backoff logic withheld additional scale-up attempts after two failed provisioning cycles (exponential backoff kicked in).
- Side-effect: client libraries retried aggressively; we saw retry amplification which magnified load on already saturated workers — saw ~3x increase in retries during the spike window.

Immediate actions taken:
- Flipped autoscaler to bypass the backoff for the Velora pool and requested immediate provisioning of 4 reserved nodes (manual override).
- Kicked a quick restart of 3 worker pods to clear stuck KV caches (trace attached: trace-span-20270607.json).
- Started redirect planning onto hosted fallback for low-risk endpoints (needs account/exec approval for blanket routing).

Need decisions:
- Approve temporary fallback routing (partial) to hosted pool (cost estimate ~ $2k/hr while active).
- Authorization to keep the 4 reserved nodes for 6 hours while we stabilize (billing & exec approval).

I'll continue monitoring; will post another update in 15.

- Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments:

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@velora.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T09:47:02Z
Subject: Re: [Urgent] Production 5xx spike and timeouts - Velora Prod - us-west-2

Thanks Marcus — added a few observations and a recommended mitigation plan:
- Observation: high-provision latency + autoscaler backoff produced transient starvation. The serving runtime showed many connections hitting qps-thresholds and token-generation timeouts when new nodes had not joined the pool.
- Short-term mitigation (fast): enable partial failover to hosted cluster for non-sensitive routes (auth-free endpoints) + reduce retry window on client side to avoid retry amplification. I can push a routing rule to divert up to 25% of traffic to hosted within 10 minutes.
- Medium-term (1–3 hours): increase autoscaler target buffer to maintain a 10% headroom and soften backoff aggressiveness for dedicated pools with production SLAs.
- Ask: Exec signoff required for emergency spend to reserve capacity and for us to initiate hosted fallback for Velora. Also recommend proactively notifying their CTO about potential SLA credit if thresholds are crossed.

I can execute the routing switch as soon as we have approval. If no response in 20 minutes, I suggest we start with a 10% fallback and inform the customer immediately.

- Neha
Director, Serving Platform — Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: CEO Leadership <leadership@redwood.ai>, Head of Sales <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, CFO <finance@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T10:05:00Z
Subject: Exec note — Velora production impact: request for emergency capacity and fallback OK

Leadership team,

TL;DR: Velora production in us-west-2 is experiencing a 5xx/429 spike due to dedicated pool GPU exhaustion compounded by autoscaler backoff. We've taken manual steps to provision reserved nodes and cleared stuck workers. Marcus and Neha recommend an immediate partial fallback to hosted pool and authorizing 4 reserved nodes for 6 hours to stabilize. Estimated emergency spend: ~$12k (6 hours at reserve + host fallback).

Why we need exec signoff:
- Risk: continued retry amplification will cause further customer outages and may trigger SLA breach.
- Cost: emergency reserved capacity and fallback routing have non-trivial hourly cost.
- External impact: Velora is a mid-market account with upcoming renewal; account team requests quick remediation and a customer-facing timeline.

Requested approvals (please reply-all with A)
1) Approve temporary partial fallback routing to hosted pool (up to 25% traffic) — needed within 15m to slow retries.
2) Approve emergency reservation of 4 nodes for 6 hours for velora-dedicated-usw2.
3) Authorize issuing a proactive SLA credit if we miss p99 latency targets today (Marissa can draft).

If I don't hear an objection in 20 minutes we will proceed with (1) and (2) and notify Velora that we are taking action.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Customer Ops — Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@velora.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-08T15:03:20Z
Subject: Velora incident update: mitigation complete and next steps

Oliver — final update after stabilization: 
- What happened: autoscaler backoff + spot/AZ provisioning variability caused node-provision delays, leading to GPU worker starvation and a burst of 5xx/429 errors. Client retries amplified the load.
- What we did: 1) Manual override to provision 4 reserved nodes (6h) to relieve immediate pressure. 2) Partial fallback routing (15%) to hosted pool for low-risk routes. 3) Restarted stuck workers and cleared KV caches. 4) Reduced client-side retry window recommendation shared with your eng team.
- Outcome: error rate returned to baseline within ~45 minutes of mitigations. p95 latency back to ~260ms.

Attached: diagnostic runbook + logs (pod-logs-20270607.txt), spans (trace-span-20270607.json), and a proposed customer SLA credit letter (sla-request-velora.pdf).

Next steps (planned):
- Platform: implement autoscaler policy change to maintain 10% headroom for dedicated pools with SLA > 99.9% (Neha).
- Account: Marissa to draft SLA credit / goodwill letter (Marissa, please share).
- Post-incident: joint RCA meeting scheduled for 2027-06-09 10:00 PT — invite will follow.

We'll remain on-call for any regression. Apologies for the disruption and thanks for the quick coordination.

— Hannah
Senior Customer Ops — Redwood Inference
